page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 virtual CPUs (2 threads per core). It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per core). Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, BMI2, ADX, and AES-NI hardware cryptography. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs. Networking relies on a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across multi-threaded operations, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded throughput. In Geekbench tests, the instance scored 1,183.0 in single-core and 4,650.0 in multi-core metrics, aligning with its middle 50% category alongside a PassMark CPU score of 7,482.86. Similarly, stress-ng multi-core testing reached 6,740.18 points. Memory bandwidth reaches 34.0 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 27.42 GB/sec for write tasks. Redis SET operations measured 6.32 million operations per second, indicating viable performance for in-memory caching under burstable constraints.

Performance trade-offs emerge in raw decompression, compression, and high-concurrency storage simulations. Single-threaded gzip compression scored in the bottom 25% at 20.35 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 17.79 GB/sec, placing it within the bottom 10%. PassMark database operations and physics tests also ranked in the lower quartile, as did static web serving throughput at 5.69 GB/sec. Small-model (135M) LLM text generation maintained an average rate of 89.06 tokens per second, but prompt ingestion fell into the bottom 25% at 301.89 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is dictated by the burstable CPU allocation model, offering high resource density of 8 vCPUs and 32 GB RAM for workloads that do not demand sustained 100% CPU utilization. Because it lacks bundled local NVMe storage and relies on network-attached storage, heavy direct I/O pipelines must account for storage latency. Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is suited for staging environments, development servers, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, and intermediate application or web serving workloads that experience variable traffic patterns.
description: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor. Hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no dedicated GPUs and features no local instance storage. Across benchmark tests, the instance records middle-tier results in multi-core CPU evaluations (PassMark score of 7,482.86, Geekbench multi-core of 4,650.0) and in-memory operations (6.32 million Redis SET ops/sec). Conversely, single-threaded throughput, file compression, and database operations rank in the lower percentiles. The burstable CPU allocation makes this configuration cost-efficient for uneven compute demands rather than sustained heavy parallel workloads. Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge fits intermittent application workloads, code compilation tasks, CI/CD runners, and medium-scale web application staging.
